english: The ship was going on the sea. Then rain-clouds were covering the sky, and the darkness became thick. Then Perkunos gave thunder. The sea was being stirred up and the water was swelling. Then the men became afraid. The rope was breaking. The ship was splitting. Then the leader cried out: 'Perkunos, rescue us!' Then they threw silver into the sea. Then the thunder went away and the clouds went away. Day dawned. They lived.
uncertain: móri (in 'h₂ŕ̥ǵn̥tom móri Hih₁ként'): bare accusative of goal, 'into the sea'
gʷíh₃wont: imperfect 3pl 'they were alive / lived'; subject = the men, implied
h₂wést: aorist 'it dawned' (impersonal); also analyzable as imperfect of another h₂wes-

english: Mother Earth, let me lie down. Mother Earth, guard me in the night. And you stars, watch over me. May the beast not eat me; may sleep take me. May my horses lie close by. May the night cover me; may the fire burn. Dawn, may I wake in your light.
uncertain: légʰoh₂: subjunctive 1sg 'let me lie down' or present 1sg 'I lie down'
spéḱyete: 2pl present, imperfect or imperative; read as imperative addressed to the stars
ḱóm: adverb 'together/near'; also analyzable as a deictic accusative 'this one'
misfit: h₂ḱh₃ih₁tā́m: optative 3rd person DUAL ('may the two eat'), but its subject ǵʰwḗr 'beast' is singular; expected 3sg h₂ḱh₃yéh₁t

english: The wolf came to the shepherd: 'Sell me a sheep.' 'I will sell you one.' Then he (the shepherd) was dressing the dog in wool. Then the wolf gave a bull and took the dog. He did not recognize the dog. Then the wolf was going to the hill carrying the dog, and he was glad. Then the dog seized the wolf and was tearing at him. He cried out and fled. The shepherd drove the bull home. Whoever deceives is himself deceived.
uncertain: woséyet: subject not stated; from context the shepherd
h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂h₁: instrumental sg 'with wool' (could also be dual)
bʰérǵʰom: accusative of goal 'to the hill'; also analyzable as imperfect 1sg of a verb, which does not fit
HréwdHt / bʰéwgt: subject = the wolf, implied
h₁ért: aorist 'arrived'; taken with accusative of goal poh₂iménm̥

english: The guest and the horse were going along the path. Then the sun was heating the two of them. They were thirsty and sweating. They were looking for water and did not find it. Then the horse went ahead and the guest followed it. Then they reached the water. It was broad. Then the horse drank, and the guest was drinking water. Then the guest sat down. Then the two had their fill. To whoever is thirsty, water is dear.
uncertain: h₂óǵmoh₁: instrumental sg 'along the path' (could also be dual)
tóh₁: accusative dual 'the two of them' (or instrumental sg)
tr̥ptā́m: aorist 3du of terp- 'be sated'; also analyzable as aorist of trep- 'turn'
h₁ést: imperfect of 'be' (also analyzable as aorist of h₁es- 'throw')

english: Day dawned. Then the man stood up and put on his shoes. Then he took gifts. His mother was cooking. Then he yoked two swift horses. Then his wife said to him: 'Go, and come home safely.' Then his father said: 'May the gods protect you.' Then he went out of the village, and the dog followed him. Then the sun came up. The sun's wheel was high. A bird was flying on ahead. Then he saw a long road. The road was long, and he was not afraid. He was seeking great fame.
uncertain: h₂éwHt: 'put on (footwear)' with no object stated
déh₃reh₂: neuter plural 'gifts' (collective)
h₂éwis: nominative 'bird'; also analyzable as genitive of h₂ówis 'sheep', which does not fit
ḱóymōd: ablative 'from the village/home'

english: The shepherd was sitting in the fold. Then [a man / of men] came to him and said: 'I give you four cows. Give me ten sheep.' Then the shepherd spoke: 'There are many sheep. Let us make an agreement. Whoever breaks the agreement, may the gods strike him down.' Then the shepherd bought four cows, and the man bought ten sheep. Then the man drove the sheep away, and the shepherd drove them (the cows) into the fold. Then the two were glad.
uncertain: sékʷt: aorist of sekʷ- 'say' here (also 'follow')
kagʰyóm: accusative of goal 'into the fold'
h₁íns: masculine acc pl, refers to the cows
kʷréyh₂t: 'acquired by trade, bought'
misfit: h₂n̥rṓm: genitive PLURAL of h₂nḗr 'man', but it stands where the subject of gʷémt 'came' is needed; expected nominative h₂nḗr (as used later in the same text)

english: A guest came along the path. Then the man saw him and stood up. Then the guest said: 'Where are you going?' He said: 'I am going home. My home is far away.' 'Who are you?' 'I am a guest.' 'What is your name?' 'My name is famous.' 'I do not know it.' Then the two sat down together. The guest gave him water, and the two ate. Then the guest spoke: 'May the gods guide you,' and he went away. The man went on.
uncertain: speakers of the dialogue are not marked; the order makes the man the one going home and the guest the one answering 'I am a guest'
déh₃t gʰóstis h₁ésmey wódr̥: grammar is clear (the guest gives the man water), though a host giving the guest water would be the expected story
h₂óǵmoh₁: instrumental sg 'along the path'
ḱlutóm: adjective 'famous'; also analyzable as aorist 2du 'you two heard'
ḱóm: adverb 'together'

english: The famous king had not seen his home for ten years. Then he came, and he was a stranger. Then the queen saw him and did not recognize him. She gave him water, and he drank it. Then he said: 'I have seen the king.' 'Where have you seen him?' 'I have seen him at sea. He is alive.' 'He is alive?' 'He will come home safely.' 'May the gods lead him home.' Then: 'I am the king. My name is famous.' The queen was looking at him, and her heart recognized him. Then tears came.
uncertain: h₁suḱléwēs: compound h₁su- 'good' + ḱléwos 'fame', 'of good fame, famous'; the analyzer does not parse it
gʰóstis-kʷe h₁ést: 'and he was a guest/stranger'
pótnih₂: 'mistress' or 'wife'; here the queen / the king's wife
ǵnéh₃t-kʷe h₁ésyeh₂s ḱḗr h₁ím: ḱḗr taken as the subject of ǵnéh₃t 'her heart recognized him'

english: Gods, protect my husband. May neither beast nor thief seize him. May the river be passable for him. May his horses be swift. Gods, may he have strength. May Perkunos not strike him. Make his path straight. May he come home safely. If he comes home safely, I will give you a gift.
uncertain: wiHróm: 'man' or 'husband'; the speaker says 'my man', so 'husband'
h₂léksete / h₃roǵéyete: 2pl present or imperative; read as imperatives to the gods
gʷm̥tóm: adjective 'passable'; also analyzable as aorist 2du
ǵʰwḗr bʰṓr-kʷe ... mē lm̥bʰih₁tā́m: dual optative fits the two subjects; 'and' after a prohibition read as 'neither ... nor'

english: The merchant and the master made an agreement. Then the master gave five horses. Then the merchant took the horses. He did not give the silver. 'Where is the silver?' 'The horses are not swift.' Then the master said: 'Whoever breaks the agreement, Father Dyeus, strike him down!' Then thunder came forth, and the merchant's house was burning. Then he became afraid. He gave it (the silver) to the master. The agreement stood.
uncertain: wesowiHrós: compound wesó- 'trade' + wiHrós 'man', 'trader, merchant'; the analyzer does not parse it
speakers of 'Where is the silver?' / 'The horses are not swift' are not marked; read as master, then merchant
h₁áyto: middle aorist 'took, received'
ḱóymos: 'home, house, village'
h₁íd: neuter, refers back to h₂ŕ̥ǵn̥tom 'silver'

english: Dawn, daughter of the sky, come to me. You who drive the stars away, who lead the wheel of the sun, who are red. Shine on my road. Dawn, shine on my horses. Dawn, bring me light. Dawn, may my heart rejoice. Dawn, lead me home. Dawn, may I see your light.
uncertain: h₂éǵesi: present 2sg 'you drive' (with h₂epó 'away'); also analyzable as subjunctive of h₂eǵ- 'say', which does not fit
h₁yéh₂: feminine relative, agrees with Dawn
méne ḱḗr mudyéh₁t: ḱḗr taken as the subject of the 3sg optative 'may my heart become glad'
léwkm̥: accusative 'light'; also analyzable as aorist 1sg

english: The sea is great. Rivers go to the sea. The sea is never filled. Fish live in the sea. Beasts do not live in the sea. No one ploughs the sea. There is no road on the sea. The ship is the road. The star shows the ship its road. The sun sank into the sea. Dawn, daughter of the sky, shone. The sea is dear to fish. The sea gives men fish and death. The sea is great.
uncertain: déh₂nuh₂ ... h₁éyti: neuter plural 'rivers' with a 3sg verb (neuter plural takes a singular verb)
kʷis ne: indefinite 'no one'
piskbʰós / h₂nr̥bʰós: dative plural 'to fish' / 'to men'
mréy séngʷt: locative 'sank in(to) the sea'

english: The path was long, and the hills were high. It was winter. Then the man was climbing a hill. Snow lay on the hills. He grew cold. His breath came out, and he grew tired. Then he saw a wolf. The beast was standing in the snow and watching him. Then the man threw a stone, and the wolf fled. Then he sat down, ate, and leaned against the stone. It grew warm, and the snow was melting. Then he saw a distant river. Then he went down.
uncertain: bʰérǵʰontes: participle-adjective 'high', plural
gʷʰért: aorist 'became warm', no subject: impersonal 'it grew warm'
ḱl̥niyó: middle imperfect 'was leaning' (with locative h₂ḱméni 'against/on the stone')
kʷelsóm: 'distant'; agrees with déh₂nu taken as neuter

english: A woman carrying washed wool came to the merchant. He saw her. Then he said: 'Is the wool good?' Then she said: 'It is good. I will sell it.' 'Give it to me. I will give you silver.' Then she gave it to him, and he gave her silver and took it. Then the two were glad. Then the merchant was buying a lot of wool and carrying it away. Then he sold it, and received much silver. Then he grew rich.
uncertain: pótnih₂: 'mistress' or 'wife'; here 'a woman / the lady'
wesowiHróm / wesowiHrós: compound 'trade-man, merchant'; the analyzer does not parse it
h₁íh₂m̥ moy dédh₃dʰi: the speaker is not marked; read as the merchant
nigʷtéh₂m: 'washed', feminine, agrees with h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m
déh₃t ... déh₃ut: subjects implied (she gave; he gave)

english: The father and his son came to the water. Then the father said: 'River, you are swift. We give you a poured offering.' Then he put the offering in the water. 'Let us cross. Do not kill us.' Then the son was trembling. The river was listening to the two of them. Then the two crossed, and the water did not seize them. Then the two stood on the far side. The father said: 'The river is unfailing.'
uncertain: ǵʰutóm: adjective 'poured (as a libation)'; also analyzable as aorist 2du
mē nos moréyes: mē with the augmentless past 2sg = prohibitive 'do not kill us'
h₁íd tóh₁ ḱléwset: h₁íd taken as the neuter river (subject), tóh₁ as accusative dual 'them two'; alternatively 'he (the son) was listening to it'
déh₂nu is treated as neuter throughout (HéHḱu, ń̥dʰgʷʰitom, h₁íd)
h₂én: 'there, on the far side'

english: The sheep and the horses.
uncertain: whole text: not in the corpus's laryngeal notation; nothing analyzes. Read by its shape as awis 'sheep', akwāsas 'horses', ka 'and'
misfit: awis akwāsas ka: whole item is in a different, laryngeal-less older orthography (awis for h₂ówis, akwāsas for h₁éḱwōs, ka for -kʷe); it does not fit the corpus language

english: Wolf and thief, flee! I am not afraid. Do not come near my horses. Fire is all around. Perkunos is above. And the earth is below. Then the fire [scorches?] the two of you. May Perkunos strike the wolf's teeth. Go away from my path!
uncertain: bʰugté / dʰgʷʰh₂té / litté: 2pl imperatives/injunctives addressed to two beings (wolf and thief), not dual; maybe meant generically

h₂ewseti: the lexicon gives no sense; parent root h₂ews- 'draw water, scoop up' (Greek αὔω reflex). The context (fire acting on them) suggests 'singes/kindles', but the 'burn' root is h₁ews-; the meaning is a guess
tóh₁: accusative dual 'those two'
mē dʰgʷʰh₂té: mē + aorist = prohibitive 'do not come near'

english: It was growing dark. Then the man sat down on the ground, and his heels were tired. Then he was making a fire. The fire was burning. It grew cold. Then many stars shone. The night was long, and the darkness was thick. Then he was looking at the stars. 'Stars, have you seen my home?' The stars did not speak. 'I remember my home. Mother Earth, guard me.' The fire died down. Then sleep took him. Then day dawned, and the sun's wheel came up. Then he woke and stood up.
uncertain: tpḗrsneh₂h₁: dual 'both heels' (subject of the 3du ḱm̥h₂tā́m)
stéwdt: aorist, no subject: impersonal 'it grew cold'
ḱrémh₂t: 'became slack', i.e. the fire died down

english: It rained. Clouds were covering the sky. Then Perkunos gave thunder. Then the river filled, and the water was rising. Then a stranger came to the water. He saw a great water. Then he said: 'I must not cross. I will build a shelter.' Then he lay down in the shelter and ate. The thunder went away, and the clouds went away. Then day dawned, and the water was no longer great. The sun shone. Then he crossed it.
uncertain: h₂wérst: aorist 'it rained', impersonal
mē péroh₂: mē + subjunctive 1sg, 'let me not cross'
h₁íd: neuter, refers back to wódr̥ 'water'

english: Two men came to the river. Then a boatman was sitting there. Then the two said: 'Boatman, [let them carry] us across.' Then he said: 'What will you give me?' 'We will give silver.' 'Sit in the boat.' Then the two gave it and sat in the boat. 'Do not be afraid.' The boatman was rowing the boat. The water was broad. Then the boatman drove the boat ahead. Then the two stood on the far side. The two spoke: 'May the gods give you good things.'
uncertain: neh₂uwiHrós / néh₂uwiHre: compound néh₂u- 'ship' + wiHrós 'man', 'boatman'; nom. and voc.; the analyzer does not parse it
h₁opéyete / déh₃womes / bʰih₂té: plural forms for the two men, not dual
h₂én: 'there, to the far side'
h₁íd: neuter, refers back to the silver
misfit: bʰérontu: imperative 3rd person PLURAL 'let them carry', but it is addressed to the singular boatman (vocative néh₂uwiHre); expected 2sg bʰére
sddʰí: 2sg imperative 'sit!' said to the two men (other forms addressed to them are plural); possible mismatch

english: A stranger who was buying wool came to the master. Then he said: 'Your wool is not good.' Then the master said: 'It is good. Look at it.' 'It is not good. It is not good. I will go away.' 'Do not go away. I will give it to you.' 'What is the price?' 'The price is not high.' Then he gave silver and took it. Then he went away. Then he came again and bought a lot of wool.
uncertain: h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂s: genitive object of the participle kʷrinh₂ónts 'buying (some) wool'
h₂ew gʷémt: h₂ew 'again/back'
speakers alternate and are not marked; read from content

english: There was darkness on the sea, and many stars shone. Then a ship was sailing. The leader was watching a star. Those other stars were moving around; that one star stood still. Then he said: 'Star, lead us. We trust you.' Then the ship was following the star. Then the sky grew red. Then [at dawn ?] the star arrived and went away. The sea shone.
uncertain: h₁énoy: 'those (yonder)', nominative plural agreeing with h₂stéres
péri: adverb 'around'
bʰebʰidʰmé: perfect 1pl 'we trust'
misfit: h₂usbʰós: dative/ablative PLURAL of 'dawn', but the clause 'h₁ludʰét ... ' needs a nominative subject; expected h₂éwsōs 'Dawn arrived' (the star then went away). As it stands, h₁ludʰét has the star as its only subject: 'the star arrived and went away'

english: The sheep said to the horses: 'It pains my heart to see a man driving horses.'
uncertain: whole text: not in the corpus's laryngeal notation; nothing analyzes. Read by its shape: akwabʰyams dat pl 'to the horses', ā wawakat 'spoke', kard 'heart', agʰnutai 'pains', mai 'me', widanti 'seeing', manum 'man', akwams acc pl 'horses', agantam 'driving'
misfit: awis akwabʰyams ā wawakat ...: whole item is in a different, laryngeal-less older orthography (awis, akwams, kard, manum); it does not fit the corpus language

english: The sheep and the horses.
uncertain: title-like fragment with no verb

english: The merchant yoked the horses. Then he put wool in the wagon. Then he went along a long road. [He crossed] rivers and hills. Then he came to a distant land. There he was a stranger. There he lived through the winter. Then he sold the wool and bought silver, a robe, and a horse. Then he put the robe in the wagon. Then he came home safely. He gave the robe to his wife. His name became famous.
uncertain: wesowiHrós: compound 'trade-man, merchant'; the analyzer does not parse it
pĺ̥h₂seh₂m: 'a type of women's garment' (robe/cloak)
kʷrinéh₂t-kʷe h₂ŕ̥ǵn̥tom pĺ̥h₂seh₂m márkom-kʷe: unclear whether silver is something he bought or what he got for the wool; only márkom carries the -kʷe
ǵʰiméni: locative 'in winter'
misfit: pr̥wé: aorist 1st person DUAL 'we two crossed', but the subject throughout is the singular merchant (3sg); expected a 3sg form

english: The driver was driving the wagon, and two swift horses were pulling it. Then the wheel was breaking. The horses stopped. Then the driver sat down and said: 'Who will build the wheel?' Then a carpenter came. He saw the split wheel. He said: 'I will build the wheel. Give me a wage.' The driver gave him a wage. The carpenter was working; he was building the wheel and greasing it with fat. Then he was setting the yoke in order. Then the driver drove the wagon away again. A carpenter's work is good.
uncertain: sth₂éh₁yont: 3pl with h₁éḱwōs (pl) for the two horses (dual was used just before)
skidtóm: adjective 'split'; also analyzable as aorist 2du
yugóm h₂réydʰet: subject implied; carpenter or driver
h₂ew: 'again' or 'away'

english: The sister was ploughing in the field. Then a man was coming along the path. She was not looking at him. Then the sister heard his step and recognized it. Her heart was trembling. She cried out: 'Brother!' Then the sister, leaving the field, ran. The brother said: 'I have come home safely, sister.' She said: 'You are dear.' Then the two went home.
uncertain: nésm̥: aorist 1sg 'I returned safely'
lewbʰós: masculine 'dear', addressing the brother
ih₂tā́m: 3du past 'the two were going'

english: A stranger saw a shepherd sitting on a hill. Then he said to him: 'Where is there water?' Then the shepherd said: 'It is over there,' and he pointed out the path. 'Go down and cross the field. Then you will see it.' Then the stranger spoke: 'Is the path long?' 'The path is not long. May the gods protect you.' Then the stranger went down.
uncertain: widḗsi: subjunctive 2sg 'you will see'
h₁íd: neuter, refers to wódr̥
pr̥dʰí: imperative of pér- 'cross'
